NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the center of the AI compute value chain, critically dependent on TSMC for advanced-node chip fabrication with virtually no alternative foundry for leading-edge GPU production. On the downstream side, NVIDIA's revenue is heavily concentrated among a handful of hyperscale cloud providers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) who collectively represent the majority of data center GPU demand, making NVIDIA both powerful and exposed to the capex cycles and in-house chip development strategies of these key customers.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the pinnacle of the consumer electronics supply chain as a fabless designer and brand owner, outsourcing manufacturing to a tightly controlled network of Asian suppliers — most critically TSMC for silicon and Samsung/LG for displays — while distributing primarily through global wireless carriers and its own retail ecosystem. Its downstream is dominated by end consumers accessed via carrier partnerships and direct channels, with Services revenue increasingly dependent on platform relationships with Google, Meta, and millions of App Store developers.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the center of the global memory supply chain, purchasing highly specialized fab equipment and materials from a concentrated set of capital equipment suppliers to manufacture DRAM and NAND at scale. Its end-market exposure spans hyperscalers, AI accelerator vendors, mobile OEMs, and automotive customers, making it a critical enabler of the AI infrastructure buildout and consumer electronics ecosystems.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM sits at the apex of the semiconductor intellectual property ecosystem, licensing CPU/GPU/NPU architectures to virtually every major chip designer rather than manufacturing silicon itself, making its upstream dependencies primarily EDA toolmakers and process node partners rather than physical material suppliers. Its downstream relationships span the entire technology industry — from mobile and PC to cloud, automotive, and IoT — with royalty revenue tied directly to the volume of ARM-based chips shipped globally by its licensees.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company sitting at the critical intersection of AI-driven data center infrastructure and network edge computing, heavily dependent on TSMC's advanced process nodes for manufacturing its custom ASICs, storage controllers, and Ethernet solutions. Its downstream revenue is increasingly concentrated among hyperscale cloud providers (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) who are driving custom silicon co-design engagements, making Marvell a key enabler of next-generation AI and cloud infrastructure buildouts.
